meta.title: Notenn
meta.description: Diatonic accordion tabs in Système Argoat: import a tune and Notenn writes the buttons, bellows and basses.

home.title: Buttons and bellows, note after note.
home.lead: Notenn turns a score or a MIDI file into a diatonic accordion tab: which button to play, which way the bellows go, and the basses, no sheet music reading needed.
home.heroCaption: “Au clair de la lune” on a G/C box: blue is push, red is draw.
home.step1: A MIDI, MusicXML or ABC file, or a tune from the library. Notenn finds the melody by itself.
home.step2: Each note becomes a button number, on the push or draw line, with the bass that goes under it.
home.step3: Listen with the cursor, slow it down, loop a passage, then download the PDF.
home.notationTitle: A notation made for the diatonic
home.notationText: Système Argoat puts push and draw on two separate lines, so you see at once when the bellows change. Rows are told apart by an apostrophe, and the staff is optional, for those who read music.
home.freeText: The workshop runs right in your browser: your files never leave your computer. Notenn lives on donations from the people who use it.

notation.title: Système Argoat
notation.lead: A diatonic accordion tab that shows at a glance which button to play and which way the bellows go.
notation.caption: Opening of “Auld Lang Syne” on a G/C box, with the staff above.
notation.bellows: Two lines: {push} for push, {pull} for draw. A number on the {push} line is played pushing, on the {pull} line drawing.
notation.rows: The number is the button’s, counted from the chin. An apostrophe (6’) means the inner row, no apostrophe the outer row; a double apostrophe (6’’) means the third row.
notation.rhythm: Numbers are placed in time: the more space, the longer the note. A dot marks each beat, a small tick the start of each bar.
notation.hold: A grey line extends the number for as long as the note is held.
notation.bass: On the bottom line, the number is a bass group: a filled circle for the bass button, an empty one for the chord. They are played in the same bellows direction as the melody.
notation.staff: Standard notation can be shown above, aligned note for note, for those who read music.
notation.why: Existing tabs often mix push and draw on a single line, with symbols to learn. Système Argoat keeps what needs no explanation: two lines, two colours, button numbers placed in time.

support.title: Support Notenn
support.lead: Notenn is free, with no ads and no account. It runs on donations.
support.costs: Donations pay for the server, the domain name and the time spent adding keyboards, tunes and new instruments.
support.liberapay: Liberapay is a non-profit platform for recurring or one-off donations, taking no commission.
support.other: Tell people about Notenn, report a fingering mistake or suggest a copyright-free tune: every bit of feedback improves the tabs for everyone.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Notenn asks for no account and sets no advertising cookie.
privacy.files: The tunes you import are read and converted in your browser. They are never sent to the server nor published.
privacy.storage: Your settings (keyboard, speed, display) and the fingerings you choose by hand are kept in your browser, on your device only. Clearing the site’s data removes them.
privacy.stats: Notenn counts visits with Umami, hosted on its own server: no cookie, no tracking from one visit to the next, no data sold. Only overall figures are kept (pages viewed, country, device type).
privacy.hosting: The site is hosted by OVH, on a server rented by the publisher.
privacy.rights: Since no personal data is collected, there is nothing to look up or delete on the server. For any question, write to the address given in the legal notice.
